name: Should I remodel the kitchen first or the bathrooms first in a whole-home renovation?

mainEntity.name: Should I remodel the kitchen first or the bathrooms first in a whole-home renovation?
mainEntity.text: Should I remodel the kitchen first or the bathrooms first in a whole-home renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no universal rule, but the best order is usually the room that creates the most disruption or has the biggest dependency on utilities and access. In many whole-home remodels, the kitchen goes first because it affects daily living and often drives the rest of the project sequencing. In others, bathrooms come first if the home will be occupied and temporary bathing access is the main concern. The right order also depends on whether one room must be completed before another trade can start elsewhere. For example, plumbing or electrical upgrades in one area may need to happen before finishes are installed in another. If the home will be vacant, the sequence can be optimized for efficiency rather than convenience. A contractor should map the critical path so you understand which rooms need to happen first and why. The best sequence is the one that reduces downtime, avoids rework, and supports the overall construction plan.
acceptedAnswer.description: Kitchen and bathrooms are often prioritized because they affect daily function and resale value, but the right order depends on dependencies, utility shutoffs, and how the home will be occupied. The most disruptive room is usually done first.
